source_interpretations.title: Give the specific IRI comparison rules precedence over the Case exclusion and apply the same comparison to signatures
source_interpretations.actor: LRS storage, equivalence comparison and signature-payload matching
source_interpretations.force: Apply the 4.2 SHALL exclusions and the 4.2.7.1 SHALL/only restrictions together
source_interpretations.conditions: Both inputs first satisfy each field's type, enumeration and syntax requirements. The field under comparison is an IRI.
source_interpretations.exceptions: Only equivalences permitted by RFC3987 §5.3.1/5.3.2. Do not infer that a string in an opaque extension value is an IRI.
source_interpretations.conclusion: The general Case exclusion does not remove the specific restrictions on IRI comparison methods. Do not equate A/a in an IRI path or mailto local part without a basis. Apply the same field-aware comparison to signature payloads and received Statements. Case mismatches in JSON keys/enumerations are validity violations before comparison.
source_interpretations.reasoning: This is ordinary scope reconciliation preserving both general and specific rules. Allowing whole-IRI lowercasing would erase only and path case distinctions. Conversely, the general Case item need not be removed entirely. Preserve the existing choice of one or more RFC3987-permitted comparison methods.
source_interpretations.delta: Previously two branches were reserved for conflict between general Case and the IRI-specific rule. Specific type rules can now take precedence, so these branches require no separate adoption choice. Remove the condition of waiting for an official correction.
allowed: Compare case differences in the same scheme/host using the selected syntax normalization.
Return 400 for a valid signature payload with a different path/local part because it is not equivalent.
forbidden: Uniformly casefolding every JSON string or every IRI.
Failing an LRS that performs correct IRI comparison solely because the old signature-equivalence-excludes-case expects 200.
source_interpretations.residual: Retain the Case exclusion for non-IRIs where compatible with each field's type and meaning. Do not introduce a Unicode casefold algorithm unspecified by the text.

source_interpretations.title: Do not reject solely for property order
source_interpretations.force: The source says may not. Derive prohibition of rejection by negating permission expressed by may; do not rewrite the source as shall not.
source_interpretations.conditions: Only JSON object member order changes; values, duplicate counts, array order and other properties remain the same.
source_interpretations.exceptions: Other independent causes such as syntax, authentication, size or malicious content remain separate. Do not extrapolate to array order.
source_interpretations.conclusion: A JSON object is an unordered collection. In the Rejection Cases context, negation of may=permission from §1.3 establishes that rejection solely for order is not permitted.
source_interpretations.reasoning: Reading this as the possibility of sometimes not rejecting contradicts both the specified permissive meaning of may and the JSON object data model. The prohibition is limited to order being the sole cause.
source_interpretations.delta: Resolve the previous reservation about negated may terminology. Neither a separate user choice nor issuer adjudication is needed.
allowed: Treat a valid Statement with reordered object members as equally valid.
forbidden: Returning 400/409 solely for object order.
Using this conclusion to ignore order differences in arbitrary arrays.
source_interpretations.residual: Reflecting actual causal discrimination in test design and the oracle is a later stage.

source_interpretations.title: Do not confuse duplicate members inside extension values with core-property violations
source_interpretations.force: The 4.2.1 SHALL rejection applies to table structure. Apply any JSON value/data structure and shall not reject in 4.2.7.2 as the specific exception.
source_interpretations.conditions: Duplicate names occur inside a grammatically valid JSON object value beneath a valid IRI key in a permitted extensions map.
source_interpretations.exceptions: Exclude repeated Statement/core properties, repeated IRI keys in the extensions map itself, malformed JSON and separate security/size reasons from this acceptance proposition.
source_interpretations.conclusion: Arbitrary JSON structure in extension values includes grammatically valid objects with duplicate members. Blanket rejection of value-internal duplicates as core/table property duplicates contradicts the specific acceptance conditions for owner-defined values. Silently changing an accepted value through last-wins is a separate issue; preserve context/result extension values without loss.
source_interpretations.reasoning: RFC8259 unique names is SHOULD, not a grammar constraint. This alone does not invalidate IEEE's duplicate prohibition. The decisive distinction is scope: each table in the introduction to 4.2.1 versus the value subtree in 4.2.7.2. Do not recursively extend table-property constraints without limit into arbitrary structures outside the tables.
source_interpretations.delta: Previously duplicate prohibition and extension acceptance were treated as sharing the same conditions. The settled proposal now distinguishes map keys from value interiors. Do not adopt last-wins as an alternative.
allowed: Reject core/map duplicates; do not reject deep extension-value duplicates solely for that reason.
Preserve duplicates using raw JSON slices or ordered member sequences (implementation is a later stage).

Compare logical equality of extension values remaining in scope as an unordered collection of decoded key/value pairs with multiplicity. For example, a:1,a:2 and a:2,a:1 differ only in object order and are equivalent. a:1,a:2 and a:2 differ in multiplicity/value and are not equivalent.
forbidden: Loading into a lossy map and returning only the first or last value.
Accepting malformed JSON on the grounds that any data structure is allowed.
Classifying an object-order-only difference between signature payload and received value as indeterminate and rejecting it.
source_interpretations.residual: The LRS does not infer owner-specific semantic equivalence beyond the supplied JSON structure, such as substitution of different keys. This does not make core/JSON structural equality unsettled. Verify cryptography against original JWS bytes; recursively compare lossless pair multisets for logical equality, retaining array order and multiplicity. Apply the explicit comparison contract rather than deferring meaning to provider selection.

source_interpretations.conclusion: For nonempty returned Statements, Last-Modified is mandatory and represents the maximum returned stored at HTTP-date second precision. dependency_contracts.title: xAPI well-formed checks and JWS validation
editions: RFC7159 (2014) for JOSE header; RFC8259 (2017) for xAPI JSON
dependency_contracts.actor: producer creates compact JWS; LRS checks xAPI well-formed; JWS recipient validates crypto when required/called
inputs: received Statement lossless JSON structure and explicit equivalence mask
optional configured verification keys and D-10 policy
rules: Compact has exactly two periods and three base64url segments; no padding/whitespace in those segments. Decode protected header as UTF-8 complete JSON object; alg is mandatory, case-sensitive and one of RS256/384/512. none/HS/ES are not xAPI permitted algorithms.

Header member uniqueness is producer MUST; receiver explicitly chooses rejection or lexically-last per RFC7515 §4. D-11 records this choice. Unknown noncritical header is ignored; an unknown/unsupported parameter listed in crit makes JWS invalid. Empty crit, listed-but-absent parameters and other producer constraints in §4.1.11 permit recipient rejection; the proposed receiver contract rejects these malformed crit uses, without relabelling that MAY as a universal receiver MUST. Do not invent a required typ/cty.

Decode payload to valid complete pre-signature Statement JSON. Required actor/verb/object and applicable structure are present. Compare logical content under SP-01/SP-03/SP-04 and preserved prior field-specific equality, not raw payload bytes or all-casefolded map.

When crypto validation is performed, use the exact ASCII protectedSegment + period + payloadSegment signing input from the received compact serialization. Never verify a reserialized header/payload. Verify RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with the alg-selected hash and RSA public key; no fallback algorithm.

RFC7518 §3.3 calls RFC3447 §8.2 and SHA-256/384/512; RSA key at least 2048 bits. Signature octet length equals modulus length; representative range, RSA verification, full EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 encoding/hash comparison all need success. RFC8017 is later information, not silent replacement for RFC3447.

x5c strings use standard base64 (§4 RFC4648), not base64url. First cert holds signer key; subsequent cert certifies previous. DER and path validation are required by RFC7515 §4.1.6; also verify JWS signature against the first key.

Without x5c, IEEE well-formed decoding/equivalence/algorithm requirements remain. A crypto not-evaluated result is distinct from valid. If a consumer asks whether JWS was successfully validated under RFC7515 §5.2, no-key/invalid-crypto cannot return success. D-10 alone decides extra nox5c admission policy.

PKIX name chaining/name constraints compare names inside the certificate path; they are not TLS endpoint-hostname checks. No automatic binding of certificate subject to the LRS endpoint hostname, Statement actor or LRS authority is introduced. xAPI authority still follows authentication/credential mapping; third-party signer may differ from actor.

RFC7515 §5.3 and §10.13: compare JSON names and string values after escape decoding, exactly unless that member explicitly defines another rule (typ/cty). Escaped alg/name spellings have the same meaning; algorithm and kid case remain significant. Preserve and compare non-BMP characters correctly (SHOULD), or reject input containing them if the underlying JSON implementation cannot do so (MUST). Never silently replace, drop or conflate characters.

The handwritten no-x5c positive requires a declared D-10 admission policy and key state. Structural-admission with unknown key may accept as crypto not-evaluated; strict verification accepts only with a known trusted key and successful verification. Known-key verification failure is rejection under both alternatives. Do not demand unconditional HTTP 200 from a strict unknown-key deployment. The existing signature-validation-context guard makes this case NOT-RUN until a capable adapter can establish these inputs; it is not itself that adapter.
outputs: payload_equivalence: equal|different (lossless structural contract, prior exclusion mask)
admission: normal-store or 400 for malformed/failed required validation; local-policy rejection labelled separately
partitions: x5c bad DER/bad leaf signature/invalid path
valid math plus invalid chain is not success
handwritten no-x5c positive: policy/key precondition or explicit capability NOT-RUN; four independent malformed negatives remain evaluable
dependency_contracts.later: Choose crypto implementation and keys, then integrate and verify against this contract after definition completion. No new primitives are silently delegated as already certified.

dependency_contracts.title: PKIX path inputs and outcomes
dependency_contracts.actor: JWS x5c recipient relying party; certificate issuer obligations are separate
inputs: prospective certification path ordered from anchor-issued certificate to signer certificate; x5c input order is leaf-first and must be converted consistently
trust-anchor input: trusted issuer name, public-key algorithm, public key, algorithm parameters; source/identity of locally configured anchor and optional constraints
validation time: current trusted time, unless an explicitly configured past-time mode is selected; not untrusted Statement.timestamp
revocation evidence per path certificate with evidence-time and status; optional extension support/capability set
intended use of leaf key and configured accepted purposes where EKU is present
rules: RFC5280 §6.1.1–6.1.6 external behavior is the contract; equivalent algorithms permitted. Chain construction is outside §6, but a complete prospective path must be supplied. n>=1, no certificate occurs twice, chain issuer/subject links and anchor binding hold. A self-signed certificate delivered as x5c is not thereby trusted. A self-signed trust anchor is an input, not a path member.

For each path certificate verify signature using current working key, current-time validity (inclusive notBefore/notAfter), non-revocation from appropriate evidence, issuer name chaining and applicable subject/SAN name constraints. Then process certificate policies, anyPolicy, mappings if supported, path length, basicConstraints CA, keyUsage keyCertSign, constraints/counters and key parameter inheritance. Process final certificate critical extensions and intersect policy tree with initial policy set before success.

Unsupported critical extension fails. Unsupported optional noncritical extension is not automatically failure; supported relevant extensions are processed. Unsupported policy mapping may be omitted only under §6.1 optional support and critical rejection boundary. A critical nondefault name-constraint min/max must be processed or rejected.

Success returns the valid policy tree, signer public key, key algorithm and parameters, with the actual input anchor/policy/time bound. Valid math alone, a matching CN alone, or nonempty x5c alone are insufficient.

RFC5280 §6.1 expressly does not require all certificates/CRLs to meet the issuing profiles in §§4/5, and recommends against adding every profile check. Keep syntax/decodability and receiver MUSTs; do not mechanically turn every CA MUST (e.g. positive short serial encoding, issuing-year convention) into mandatory LRS rejection.

If KU/EKU present, key use must be permitted by them. There is no xAPI-issued universal codeSigning/serverAuth/emailProtection OID. RFC5280 §4.2.1.3 distinguishes digitalSignature (authentication/integrity) from nonRepudiation, renamed contentCommitment (non-repudiation service). It allows digitalSignature and/or nonRepudiation for objects other than certificates/CRLs: digitalSignature bit alone is not universally mandatory for xAPI JWS. The intended service and certificate policy determine compatible KU/EKU; keyCertSign/cRLSign alone does not authorize this payload use. Intended use/allowed purposes is a named security configuration input, not a random purpose selected by the adapter. Any additional mandatory EKU presence is local policy.

Certificate validity parsing uses PKIX UTCTime/GeneralizedTime representations and two-digit year pivot 50 (1950–2049). PKIX profile timezone/seconds/fraction rules are retained, with issuer profile vs receiver support separated. Already-authorized date-time arithmetic delegation remains usable; these PKIX calling constraints are not delegated away.

RFC5280 §4.1.2.2: certificate users MUST handle serialNumber values up to 20 content octets without truncation, binary64/int64 identity collapse or overflow. CA length/positive-serial obligations are separate; a nonpositive or longer issuer deviation alone does not establish a universal receiver rejection rule.

RFC5280 §4.2: the mandatory extension recognition floor is keyUsage, certificatePolicies, subjectAltName, basicConstraints, nameConstraints, policyConstraints, extendedKeyUsage and inhibitAnyPolicy. authorityKeyIdentifier, subjectKeyIdentifier and policyMappings recognition is SHOULD, with the explicit §6.1 mapping-support/critical-extension boundary retained. Recognition includes the applicable semantics, not merely accepting the OID. Do not label the eight mandatory forms optional.
outputs: VALID with key/policy-tree and full input identity
INVALID with first normative failure reason
INDETERMINATE when a necessary key/path/status/time input is unavailable; never upgraded to VALID; IEEE-required x5c validation has not succeeded
partitions: untrusted anchor vs trusted configured anchor
name constraints for each name form
policy intersection empty with explicit policy required
dependency_contracts.later: Anchor values, actual clock and evidence feed are runtime configuration inputs, not unanswered source semantics. Baseline provider may use pre-provisioned path/CRL data. Optional remote retrieval needs its own transport contract before enabling; it is not a prerequisite imposed on this local-input contract.

dependency_contracts.title: Revocation checks and CRL conditions
dependency_contracts.actor: path validator consumes evidence; CRL issuer publishes signed CRLs
inputs: mechanism = CRL | independently trusted status service | out-of-band trusted status
for CRL: distribution point, reason coverage, complete CRL and optional delta CRL, issuer path and issuer key
use-deltas flag; evidence freshness and authenticity inputs
rules: Path basic check requires certificate not revoked. RFC5280 permits CRLs, status information, or out-of-band mechanisms; it does not require online CRL network access for every request. No evidence/unknown is not not-revoked.

When CRLs are used, follow §6.3: issuer/distribution-point/issuingDistributionPoint applicability; cert type restrictions; reason masks; CRL issuer key/path to same trust anchor and cRLSign KU if present; verify CRL signatures and time currency. Scope/issuer match is essential, not only serial match.

If using delta, match issuer/issuingDistributionPoint/authority key, delta/base numbers and validity association; process delta entry then complete CRL, including certificateIssuer and removeFromCRL. Accumulate reasons across applicable CRLs. Only complete applicable coverage without revocation yields UNREVOKED; absence from a partial/unrelated/stale list does not.

RFC5280 profile requires issuer nextUpdate and defines algorithm currency assumptions; client behavior for omitted nextUpdate is not completely specified in §5.1.2.5. This contract treats missing freshness information as INDETERMINATE unless an independently trusted freshness contract supplies it. It does not assert all such issuer deviations are mandatory certificate-format rejection.

For a status-service or out-of-band input, the input contract must attest certificate+issuer binding, authenticated source, validation-time coverage, and good/revoked/unknown. This proposal does not claim a wire OCSP implementation; enabling OCSP or remote transport adds its referenced protocol review and integration, not a silent substitute.

A current authentic applicable complete CRL may have revokedCertificates absent because it contains no revoked entries. With valid signer/path/usage/signature, complete applicable reason coverage and no applicable revocation, this is sufficient UNREVOKED evidence. It is distinct from no CRL evidence, an empty cache, stale/unrelated CRLs and incomplete reason coverage.

RFC5280 §5.2.3: CRL verifiers MUST handle CRLNumber values up to 20 content octets. Compare CRLNumber and delta/base number relations exactly; do not collapse neighboring large integers. The issuer maximum-length requirement does not by itself define universal receiver rejection outside this guaranteed capacity.
partitions: valid negative coverage all reasons; partial reasons
CRL signature bad or CRL signer path/KU invalid
dependency_contracts.later: Supply actual trusted evidence and prove adapter integration later. No network-fetch requirement is added to the user’s definition phase.

dependency_contracts.title: Certificate-name comparison and constraints
editions: RFC4518 (2006) with explicitly considered Verified errata
X.501:2005 §9.3 legal Name input boundary; not whole Directory-stack incorporation
dependency_contracts.actor: PKIX recipient compares names; CA encodes names
inputs: permitted/excluded subtree sets by name form
rules: Mandatory DirectoryString support is UTF8String and PrintableString. Support for Teletex/BMP/UniversalString is optional under §7.1; unsupported required-to-compare names cannot yield a valid path. RFC5280 supplies standard attribute OIDs/syntax and Name/RDN structures; X.500/501/509/520:2005 are informative origins, not a requirement to implement Directory services.

DN preparation follows RFC4518 six steps using stored values: transcode, map, Unicode3.2 NFKC, prohibit, bidirectional treatment (RFC4518 explicitly ignores bidi here), insignificant-space handling. Case folding uses RFC3454 B.2. Do not reuse IDNA nameprep or a modern runtime’s default Unicode casefold. Prepare both attribute values; type OID equal and prepared values equal. RDN is unordered collection; DN is ordered sequence; subtree uses RDN prefix.

RFC4518 erratum860 (Verified) corrects impossible FF00–FE0F to FE00–FE0F. Apply this correction in proposed contract, explicitly not a modification of RFC bytes. Errata1757/1758 concern substring handling, not stored-value non-substring DN equality. Editorial7213/9048 do not alter this contract.

DirectoryString non-substring insignificant-space handling is precise: entirely-space input becomes two spaces; otherwise ensure one leading and one trailing space and compress internal nonempty space runs to two spaces. Ignore no arbitrary punctuation or accents.

dNSName and domainComponent in certificates are ASCII/IA5 encoded. CA IDN conversion is RFC3490 ToASCII per label, AllowUnassigned=false and UseSTD3ASCIIRules=true; recognize defined dot variants and output U+002E. Compare encoded DNS labels case-insensitively with label boundaries. RFC3491 uses Unicode3.2 B.1/B.2/NFKC/prohibited tables and bidi; RFC3492 Punycode parameters and fail-on-overflow/truncation are fixed.

rfc822Name mailbox local part is exact and host case-insensitive. Mail name constraints can select a mailbox, exact host, or leading-dot domain; do not global-lowercase mailboxes. Legacy subject emailAddress is constrained when rfc822Name constraints apply and SAN absent.

Certificate URI names: IA5, IRI converted per §7.4; RFC3987 syntax-based and scheme-based normalization are required, with http/https/ftp/ldap treatment in §7.4. This differs from xAPI data IRI’s only §5.3.1/5.3.2 restriction. URI name constraints apply to DNS host; missing/non-DNS authority under URI constraints fails. DNS subtree, directoryName subtree and IP network+mask constraints are different algorithms.

For certificate URI comparison, the mandatory scheme step removes empty/default ports (http=80, https=443, ftp=21, ldap=389) and normalizes an empty authority-path to /. Keep userinfo, query and fragment delimiters unless the scheme explicitly licenses removal. LDAP uses RFC4516 §3 general defaults where no overriding context exists (empty DN, all user attributes, base scope, objectClass=* filter, no extensions); omitted vs explicitly default fields compare equally. No implicit directory lookup, host substitution, filter evaluation, FTP login, guessed transfer type, server-specific path case-folding or redirect equivalence is added. Reserved escaped separators remain significant. LDAP DN/filter semantic alias resolution is beyond the RFC3987 §5.3.3 normalization call, not silently required as a full LDAP client.

Unknown attribute DirectoryString values MAY use §7.1 preparation; non-DirectoryString unfamiliar values use binary comparison recommendation. No arbitrary unknown extension/otherName semantic interpretation is claimed. Critical unsupported constraints fail, supported noncritical relevant constraints are processed.

RFC5280 §4.1.2.4 calls the domainComponent attribute defined by RFC4519 §2.4. A conforming stored value is one ASCII LDH label of 1..63 characters, with alphanumeric edges; comparison is case-insensitive. The storing party is responsible for the label restriction; retain the stored/query ToASCII profile distinction. This input-domain clarification is not a new blanket LRS HTTP rejection rule or a requirement to implement an LDAP directory.

RFC5280 defines Name through X.501:2005. For legal RDN inputs, X.501 §9.3 permits each attribute type only once within an RDN. Keep that boundary when applying same-count/type/prepared-value matching and unordered RDN versus ordered DN comparison. Generic SET OF alone does not imply uniqueness; DER-decodable duplicate-type input is not a positive legal-Name control and does not acquire an invented universal HTTP rejection.

Later provider evidence: UAX15 revision22 Annex9 calls the fixed Unicode3.2 normalization conformance data. A provider claiming the NFKC contract must satisfy the frozen NormalizationTest-3.2.0 column invariants (all c1..c5 normalize to c4 for NFKC). This defines a future provider-verification obligation, not current execution, a new xAPI HTTP oracle, or certification of every Unicode table entry.
outputs: unsupported/unpreparable result cannot be promoted to path success

RDN permutation vs DN sequence change
ASCII DNS case and boundary vs lookalike
URI host/default-port normalization distinct from xAPI IRI
IP mask match vs address prefix string error

dependency_contracts.title: ASN.1/DER editions and receiving contract
editions: RFC5280 Appendix A hybrid 1988/1993 notation; its explicit schema is authoritative here
dependency_contracts.actor: DER/PKIX decoder, not ASN.1 schema author or full X.500 stack
inputs: RFC5280 Certificate/TBSCertificate/Name/Extension schema; AlgorithmIdentifier-dependent parameter schema
CRL CertificateList/TBSCertList schema if CRL mechanism used
RSA SubjectPublicKeyInfo/key and signature OIDs for supported algorithms
rules: Use type-aware tag/class/constructed-bit/definite-length decoding. DER requires minimal definite length and minimal two’s-complement INTEGER, primitive bit/octet/restricted-character strings, TRUE=FF and FALSE=00, unused BIT STRING bits zero, named-bit-list trailing zero treatment, DEFAULT component omission, SEQUENCE order and canonical SET/SET OF order. OID components use minimal base128 encoding and combined first two arcs.

EXPLICIT wrapping and IMPLICIT tag replacement follow the RFC5280 module defaults and X.680 tagging semantics. CHOICE uses selected alternative tag; unknown ANY is interpreted only by its OID-defined type. The typed schema, not arbitrary TLV shape, determines validity.

PKIX signed material is original DER TBSCertificate/TBSCertList, not reconstructed normalized bytes. Extension extnValue is OCTET STRING containing DER of its OID-defined type. Preserve unknown noncritical extension bytes and distinguish unsupported critical extension.

X.6902002 §§10–11 and X.6902008 §§10–11 agree for the certificate types actually used (minimal lengths, string form, boolean, unused bits, defaults, set order, UTC/GeneralizedTime). Section numbering changes for character strings and later time types do not substitute new certificate schema. Both exact editions are pinned; no latest-edition resolution is left to the adapter.

X.6802002 universal tags and PrintableString alphabet are read and visually checked. RFC5280 Appendix B identifies RFC3629 as the definition of UTF8String used in Appendix A, limiting accepted octets to valid Unicode scalar encoding. IA5String is 7-bit; PrintableString is the listed subset, not arbitrary Unicode.

X.690 DER time encoding requires Z and seconds; generic DER GeneralizedTime can have canonical nonzero fractions, while the RFC5280 issuer profile disallows fractional seconds for certificate validity. Keep that profile/receiver distinction rather than globally certifying or rejecting every CA deviation.

RFC3279 §2.3.1 fixes RSA SPKI rsaEncryption OID and DER sequence(n,e), with NULL parameters. RFC4055 defines SHA256/384/512 RSA signature OIDs and requires receivers to accept NULL or absent signature AlgorithmIdentifier parameters. Restricted RSA-PSS/OAEP key OIDs cannot silently be used as unrestricted RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 keys.

No claim to full ASN.1 compiler, CER, PER, XML, X.400 names, legacy Teletex decoder, or all certificate-signature algorithms. Necessary standard PKIX types and mandatory name forms are covered; additional optional capability must be declared and reviewed before use. Cannot hide a mandatory certificate path check behind this optional boundary.

INTEGER canonical encoding and typed-domain validity are separate: 02 02 00 80 is +128 and 02 01 80 is canonical -128. Redundant encodings 02 02 00 7F and 02 02 FF 80 violate minimal INTEGER encoding. A changed sign can be a value mismatch or typed-domain failure without being generic DER failure; issuer serial-number profile checks remain separate.

X.690(2002/2008) §8.8: NULL is primitive and has zero content octets (05 00). A nonempty or constructed NULL is invalid for that type. Keep the RSA OID-specific distinction between absent parameters and a present NULL; do not require NULL presence for every AlgorithmIdentifier.

rules: Top-level xAPI multipart is multipart/mixed with boundary parameter. All parts have delimiter, header block, empty line and body; close-delimiter ends final part. Boundary is 1..70 permitted chars, no trailing space, case-sensitive; quotes in header are delimiters, not boundary bytes.

Parse field names and MIME type/subtype/parameter names case-insensitively. Parameter values retain their type-specific case; boundary is case-sensitive. RFC822 structured-field comments, quoted-pair and folding apply in header grammar, not inside arbitrary tokens or multipart-body BNF.

Unfold only CRLF followed by SP/HTAB within header fields. Handle nested comments and quoted strings per RFC822; header colon separates field-name/value. Do not interpret From/Date/MIME-Version as mandatory part fields. Part is not a complete RFC822 message.

RFC2046 requires ignoring preamble/epilogue, recognizing outer delimiters in nested MIME, and treating CRLF before delimiter as framing rather than previous raw part data. Transport padding is accepted as specified; sender must not generate it. Attachment raw bytes may themselves contain CRLF and non-ASCII bytes.

First xAPI part Content-Type must explicitly denote application/json because generic missing-type default is text/plain. Decode JSON with applicable UTF8/xAPI body rules. Additional parts represent raw attachment data: producer/output includes X-Experience-API-Hash and Content-Transfer-Encoding:binary as IEEE specifies; receiver SHOULD assume binary. Metadata contentType/length checks apply when the corresponding metadata/header data are provided as specified.

IEEE attachment SHA-2 rules, content length in octets, dedup/shared raw rules, missing-fileUrl handling and required returned raw completeness remain in force. Metadata array order decision D-09 does not change MIME part matching by hash or permit dropped raw data.

RFC2046 generic MIME permits nested multipart; an attachment whose raw content is itself multipart remains byte-preserved for IEEE hash matching. Do not flatten it into xAPI attachments. No SMTP delivery, mail-address parsing, message/rfc822 rendering, MIME encoded-word display, base64 MIME transport, or RFC2231 parameter extensions are introduced by this baseline. Extra part headers remain opaque unless IEEE or called MIME grammar assigns them meaning.

RRF-02: Before comment removal, validate all part header octets as US-ASCII and physical line endings as CRLF. Unfold only CRLF followed by SP/HTAB, preserving that LWSP. Bare CR/LF, non-ASCII hidden in comments, orphan continuation and invalid field names are invalid. Retain RFC822 ctext/quoted-pair distinctions; do not invent an ASCII-control blanket prohibition beyond that grammar.

RRF-03: boundary is 1..70 bchars with final bcharsnospace: alphanumeric or apostrophe, parentheses, + _ , - . / : = ?, and interior SP. A body-part line must not start with --boundary even if followed by non-delimiter text. A boundary-like substring away from line start or not sharing the chosen prefix is permitted. Preserve preamble/epilogue, transport-padding receiver allowance, and raw trailing CRLF.

RRF-07: IEEE undated FIPS180-2 incorporation includes its Change Notice 1 SHA-224. Attachment full SHA-224 is 56 hex digits; SHA-256/384/512 are 64/96/128. Use the matching full algorithm, not arbitrary truncation or SHA-512/224. This does not add any JWS algorithm beyond RS256/384/512.

RRFR-01: Within one multipart observation, retain unavailable length comparison and continue independently decidable matching metadata, Content-Type, Content-Length, later parts/headers/digests, required metadata-to-data coverage and expected raw-data checks. Return unavailable only after all safely decidable checks succeed; neither numeric widening nor provider integration is a prerequisite for comparing known media-type strings.

RRFR-F01: With an established outer multipart boundary, retain ORACLE-UNAVAILABLE from first-part media-type parsing and attachment metadata/part media-type equivalence as local unknowns, just as for length. Continue independently delimited JSON/metadata processing and subsequent Content-Length, headers/hash/CTE, raw coverage and expected-data checks. A known violation remains FAIL; return unavailable only if no independent violation is established. Keep duplicate-parameter disposition unavailable, not invalid or accepted. Ordinary lexical errors and known type mismatches remain FAIL. Top-level media-type parsing with an unresolved boundary cannot supply safe part boundaries and may return unavailable before boundary-dependent checks.

FFCR-01: MIME parsing retains independently known essence and parameter presence even if duplicate-parameter values are undecidable. Wrong multipart/first-part essence, absent boundary and definite syntax violations are FAIL before an unknown return. A unique boundary permits later checks despite unrelated parameter ambiguity; an ambiguous boundary never supplies guessed framing. Preserve the prior part-level aggregation.

FFCR-03: Generic IEEE metadata readback compares complete per-item associations and multiplicity, permitting the D-09 ordering alternatives while no policy is selected. Missing/duplicated/reassociated metadata fails; extension-owned arrays remain ordered. Exact attachment order is a separate selected-policy check, never silently imposed.

FFRR-08: Compare independently known parameter values before an unrelated duplicate-parameter unknown. RFC2046 text/plain absent charset means US-ASCII. Explicit differing charset is a known difference despite duplicate x. Do not assume this default for other subtypes, nor default arbitrary extension parameters. Compare boundary presence as a framing distinction only for multipart. Unresolved subtype/extension parameter semantics remain unknown after known comparisons.

FFSR-06: MIME parameter values use their recognized type/subtype-specific comparison rules. RFC2045/RFC2046 message/external-body access-type is case-insensitive; multipart boundary is case-sensitive and text charset is case-insensitive. Unrecognized parameters are ignored as RFC2045 requires. A recognized parameter with an unimplemented comparison is not an unrecognized parameter: retain unavailable pending its defined comparison contract. Do not turn a difference of opaque values into a known mismatch. Continue independent essence/charset/boundary/length/hash checks; a known violation dominates unavailable.
